sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.

The petitioner is arrayed as accused No.13 in Crime No.50/2018 (C.C. No.1874/2023) on the file of learned Civil Judge and JMFC Court,
Shorapur, Yadgiri District.
The case is registered based on the compliant lodged by the Chief Executive Officer, Shorapur Taluka Panchayat.

In the complaint, it is alleged that, all the accused persons in connivance with each other have NC: 2023:KHC-K:7460 misappropriated a sum of Rs.1,82,88,485/-, which was released for various development works, without completing the work entrusted to them.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, petitioner is innocent, he has not committed any offence, the alleged offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, there are no specific allegations against petitioner and the main allegation is against accused Nos.1 to 3 only.
The present complaint has been lodged in respect of not maintaining the documents properly.
If remaining 33 projects are not completed, it is a question of trial.
The petitioner is ready to abide by any conditions to be imposed by this Court, thus prays to grant bail.

4. The learned High Court Government Pleader submits that, petitioner is absconding and he is involved in non-bailable offences; the petitioner and others have misappropriated a sum of Rs.1,82,88,485/- and caused NC: 2023:KHC-K:7460 loss to State exchequer, thus she prayed for rejection of the petition.
5. Having regard to the nature of allegations made against petitioner and as said accused persons are required to be substantiated only through documentary evidence.
As per contents of charge sheet, the petitioner and others were required to complete in all 180 projects for the period from 2016 to 2018.

Out of 180 projects, 33 projects are not completed, and hence, the complainant lodged the complaint alleging that in respect of remaining 33 projects, accused Nos.1 to 3 have not maintained the documents properly.
The complainant has not made any allegations against the present petitioner, who is accused No.13.

If, accused Nos.1 to 3 have not maintained the documents Lalasab vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173469416/
2 properly, it is a matter of trial and it requires to be substantiated only through documentary evidence.

sentences.text: As per charge sheet, accused No.7, 8, 9 and 11 are already enlarged on bail.
Now investigation is completed and charge sheet is laid in the month of February 2023.

Considering the nature of allegations, circumstances in which the offences are committed,
position and status of the petitioner, likelihood of accused fleeing away from justice, or repeating same offences by the petitioner, tampering with witnesses, character and antecedents of the petitioner and fact that accused Nos.7 to 9 and 11 are already enlarged on bail, and this Court granted bail in favour of accused No.7 in Crl. P. No.201471/2018 dated 20.12.2018 and therefore on the ground of parity also, the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail, as accused No.7 and accused No.13 stands on same footing.

7. Hence, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigation Officer within 10 days from the date of this order and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions;
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7460 1.
The petitioner shall not threaten the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
